description:
Prevent JWT Token Exposure in URL Query Parameters

The OAuth callback handler in `backend/src/app/api/v1/auth.py` (line 374) redirects with JWT tokens as URL query parameters:
```python
params = urlencode({"access_token": tokens.access_token, ...})
return RedirectResponse(url=f"{redirect_url}?{params}")
```

This exposes tokens in:
- Browser history (user can see auth tokens by browsing history)
- Server access logs (HTTP referrer header includes full URL with tokens)
- Proxy/CDN caches
- Browser developer tools

Fix Implementation:
1. Implement Post-Redirect-Get (PRG) pattern:
   - Store tokens in secure server-side session or Redis
   - Redirect to callback URL with session ID only
   - Frontend retrieves tokens from secure HTTP-only cookie or session
2. OR use Fragment identifier (hash): tokens in #anchor are not sent to server
3. Ensure tokens are transmitted in HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite cookies

Example:
```python
# Generate session token, store tokens in Redis with TTL
session_id = str(uuid4())
await redis.setex(f"oauth:{session_id}", 300, json.dumps(tokens))
return RedirectResponse(url=f"{redirect_url}?session={session_id}")
```
